issues.location: Products with 50+ reviews convert at 2-3x the rate of those without (Bazaarvoice / Spiegel Research)
issues.explanation: This is a debunked benchmark. Spiegel Research found that 5 reviews (not 50+) produced a 270% conversion lift. The '50+ reviews convert at 2-3x' figure is a misrepresentation of the actual finding and is flagged as fabricated regardless of attribution.

issues.location: Average AOV uplift with cross-sell is 8-15% (Baymard Institute)
issues.explanation: Baymard Institute has never published a benchmark stating 8-15% AOV uplift from cross-sell. This is a fabricated attribution to Baymard and is on the explicit debunked-stats list.

issues.location: Unique product descriptions increase organic traffic per PDP by 30-50% (Ahrefs)
issues.explanation: Ahrefs has never published a study showing unique product descriptions increase traffic by 30-50% per PDP. This is a fabricated benchmark on the explicit debunked-stats list.

issues.location: Rich snippets increase CTR by 20-40% (Search Engine Journal / Ahrefs)
issues.explanation: Search Engine Journal is a generic industry blog, not a peer-reviewed or primary research source. Attributing a specific CTR benchmark to it alongside Ahrefs (a vendor blog) does not meet the standard for a credible business intelligence or industry benchmark citation.

issues.location: Companies with active blogs generate approximately 55% more visitors (HubSpot)
issues.explanation: HubSpot is a vendor with commercial interest in promoting content marketing. Their self-published blog statistics are widely considered unreliable industry benchmarks and fall into the category of generic blog/vendor content rather than credible third-party research.

issues.location: Coppel hold those positions... and Coppel also compete for the same branded traffic
issues.explanation: Coppel is not a sister brand of Italika/Grupo Salinas, so this specific check does not apply here. However, reviewing the report: Elektra is referenced as sharing the same VTEX instance and backend with Italika (both under Grupo Salinas), yet Elektra marketplace pages are discussed as inherited infrastructure rather than listed as a competitor — this is handled correctly. No sister-brand competitor misclassification is present.

issues.location: Italika holds a dominant position in Mexico's motorcycle market, selling approximately 1.3 million units in 2025 — the 8th largest motorcycle manufacturer globally, according to industry data.[^biz1]
issues.explanation: The citation [^biz1] resolves to imotorbike.com, a third-party motorcycle news site. While a source is provided, the specific claim of '8th largest motorcycle manufacturer globally' is a very precise ranking from a non-authoritative source that cannot be independently verified from the URL provided. This is borderline; the presence of a citation mitigates severity, but the source quality is weak for such a specific global ranking claim.

summary: The report contains three high-severity fabricated benchmarks (Baymard AOV uplift, Ahrefs unique-description traffic lift, Spiegel 50+ reviews claim) that are on the explicit debunked-stats list, plus two weak-source citations (HubSpot, Search Engine Journal); the Deloitte stat is correctly quoted, no WAF screenshots or currency confusion were found, and no sister-brand competitor misclassification is present.
